one_liner: SIMD-accelerated, ABI-compatible replacement for IJG libjpeg; the vendor says 2-6x faster JPEG encode and decode.
what_it_does: A lossy and lossless JPEG codec (8-bit lossy, 12-bit lossy, 2-16-bit lossless, Huffman and arithmetic coding, baseline and progressive) that implements the libjpeg v6b API and ABI. It can also be built to emulate the v7 or v8 ABI (-DWITH_JPEG7/-DWITH_JPEG8), so existing libjpeg programs relink or swap the shared library without source changes. It also ships the simpler in-memory TurboJPEG 3 API (tj3Init, tj3Compress8, tj3Decompress8, YUV-plane and lossless-transform functions) plus cjpeg/djpeg/jpegtran/tjbench. It is an ISO/IEC and ITU-T reference implementation of JPEG, and its ChangeLog notes it is now 'used by most operating systems'.
how_it_is_fast: Hand-written SIMD modules (NASM for x86 SSE2/AVX2, intrinsics for Arm Neon, PowerPC AltiVec, Loongson MMI and RISC-V Vector) replace the libjpeg C paths for color conversion, chroma down/upsampling (including merged upsampling plus color conversion), integer sample conversion and quantization, accurate-integer forward and inverse DCT, and the baseline and progressive Huffman encoders. A runtime dispatcher picks the best instruction set per instance. Huffman decoding is not SIMD but uses an optimized table-lookup fast path in C, which is where most of the gain on non-SIMD systems comes from. Only 8-bit-per-sample lossy paths are vectorized (simd/README.md).
when_to_use: Any C or C++ program that links IJG libjpeg (v6b, or v7/v8 through ABI emulation) and wants faster JPEG encode/decode with no code changes.
Server-side thumbnailing, image proxies and photo pipelines that decode or encode many 8-bit baseline or progressive JPEGs, one image per thread.
Decoding straight into RGBX/BGRA/XRGB buffers or planar YUV (TurboJPEG tj3DecompressToYUV8), or decoding at 1/2 and 1/4 scale (SIMD-accelerated IDCT scaling) for previews.
Lossless JPEG transforms (rotate, flip, crop, drop) through jpegtran or tj3Transform without re-encoding.
Portable deployments across x86-64, Arm64, PowerPC, Loongson and RISC-V, where one codebase gets SIMD on each.
when_not_to_use: Latency of a single large image on an idle many-core machine: libjpeg-turbo decodes one image on one thread; the catalogued jpeg-nitro decodes one baseline JPEG on all cores (about 9x lower wall time on 16 threads in its README).

Smallest files per quality: it has no trellis quantization (mozjpeg, a libjpeg-turbo fork, adds it) and no adaptive quantization (google/jpegli, also libjpeg62 API/ABI-compatible, advertises it); when bytes matter more than encode speed, evaluate those instead.

12-bit lossy or 2-16-bit lossless JPEG and arithmetic-coded JPEG throughput: those paths run in C only (issue #199, 'Performance improvements (SIMD extensions) for 12-bit JPEGs', is open with 'funding needed').

Code that needs the libjpeg v9 ABI, SmartScale, DCT scaling in the compressor or lossless RGB JPEG from IJG v9: not supported, and cinfo.scale_num/scale_denom and cinfo.block_size are silently ignored.
Targets that need AVX-512, Arm SVE2 or WebAssembly SIMD paths: all are open 'funding needed' issues (#732, #860, #250), so wasm builds fall back to C.

integration.form: shared lib or static lib (libjpeg API library libjpeg.so/jpeg-static and TurboJPEG API library libturbojpeg.so/turbojpeg-static); built with CMake
integration.dependencies: none at runtime; build needs CMake 3.15+ and NASM 2.13+ or Yasm 1.2.0+ for the x86 SIMD code (libspng and zlib are bundled for cjpeg/djpeg and tj3LoadImage/tj3SaveImage PNG support)
integration.min_toolchain: C compiler: GCC 4.1+ or Clang on Un*x, Visual C++ 2005+ or MinGW on Windows; Arm builds need GCC 12+ or Clang for full Neon performance since 3.2 (the GAS Neon code was removed)
integration.platforms: x86 and x86-64 (SSE2, AVX2), Arm 32/64 (Neon), PowerPC (AltiVec), Loongson MIPS64 (MMI), RISC-V 64 (RVV); any other CPU through the C code
integration.thread_safety: Per-instance: each jpeg_compress_struct/jpeg_decompress_struct or tjhandle must be used by one thread at a time (not stated as a rule in the files read, follows from the stateful API); since 3.2 the SIMD capability list is per instance, so no thread-local storage is needed, but tj3GetErrorStr(NULL) for global functions is thread-safe only where TLS exists (turbojpeg.h).

gotchas: Restart markers switch the decoder to the slow Huffman path for the whole image (README: up to 20% slower). Issue #910 showed a 1.08x decode gain on 25 restart-marker camera JPEGs (Ryzen 7 5800X) by limiting the slow path to restart boundaries; it was closed 'won't implement'.

The fast integer forward DCT at quality 98-100 cannot use the SIMD quantizer and runs up to 40% slower; the ChangeLog (3.0 beta2) also says the fast DCT/IDCT fail the ISO compliance tests and are no faster than the accurate ones on modern x86, so TurboJPEG 3 defaults to the accurate algorithms.
Valgrind and MemorySanitizer report false uninitialized reads in the SIMD code; set JSIMD_FORCENONE=1 at run time or build with -DZERO_BUFFERS=1 when running memory checkers.

When decompressing to RGBX/BGRX/XBGR/XRGB the X byte is left undefined for speed; use the RGBA/BGRA/ABGR/ARGB colorspaces if you need 0xFF alpha. Decompressing 4:4:0 and the float IDCT can differ slightly from libjpeg v6b output.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick libjpeg-turbo when you need the standard C libjpeg/TurboJPEG ABI, the widest set of SIMD architectures and full format coverage (progressive, arithmetic, 12-bit, lossless, transforms); libjpeg-turbo-rs and zenjpeg are Rust re-implementations that report slightly faster decode on their own x86 tests, and jpeg-nitro beats it only on single-image multi-core latency for baseline JPEGs to YCbCr planes.
verified_claims_summary: First-party only: the README says 'generally 2-6x as fast as libjpeg, all else being equal' with no machine, compiler or libjpeg version; the per-platform tables (libjpeg v6b and v8d baselines, tjbench Mpixels/s) live on libjpeg-turbo.org, which was not reachable, and tjbench itself times a 1 s warm-up and then at least 5 s of repeated compress/decompress calls and reports Mpixels/s. Third-party runs do not use IJG libjpeg as baseline: jpeg-nitro's README (Intel i9 13th gen) puts libjpeg-turbo 3.1.2 at parity with its own one-thread decoder, and google/decoder-benchmarks-for-rust (2.6 GHz 6-core Core i7, macOS) has turbojpeg at 84.25 ms versus 126.2 ms for the Rust jpeg-decoder crate on a 2000x3000 JPEG.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-25, release 3.2.0 on 2026-06-30 with 3.2.1 fixes in the ChangeLog, CVE fixes such as CVE-2026-75466 handled promptly) and permissively licensed (IJG plus Modified BSD, SIMD code under Zlib); it is the ISO/ITU-T JPEG reference implementation and the default system libjpeg on most platforms, so usability is copyable with no caveats beyond the usual BSD/IJG attribution.
